claim: B-cell repertoires are characterized by a diverse set of receptors of distinct specificities generated through two processes of somatic diversification: V(D)J recombination and somatic hypermutations.
source: B-cell repertoires are characterized by a diverse set of receptors of distinct specificities generated through two processes of somatic diversification: V(D)J recombination and somatic hypermutations.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about B-cell biology.

claim: B-cell clonal families stem from the same V(D)J recombination event, but differ in their hypermutations.
source: B-cell clonal families stem from the same V(D)J recombination event, but differ in their hypermutations.
evidence: This is a definition based on established understanding of clonal family structure.

claim: HILARy combines probabilistic models that capture the receptor generation and selection statistics with adapted clustering methods to achieve consistently high inference accuracy.
source: HILARy combines probabilistic models that capture the receptor generation and selection statistics with adapted clustering methods to achieve consistently high inference accuracy.
evidence: This is a claim about the method's design and performance, supported by the benchmark results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The statistics of evolutionary properties such as the site frequency spectrum and dN/dS ratio do not depend on the junction length.
source: Exploiting the high sensitivity of the method, we find the statistics of evolutionary properties such as the site frequency spectrum and dN/dS ratio do not depend on the junction length.
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis shown in Figure 7B and 7C.

claim: A broad range of selection pressures spanning two orders of magnitude exists in B-cell repertoires.
source: We also identify a broad range of selection pressures spanning two orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is supported by the distribution of dN/dS ratios shown in Figure 7C.

claim: V(D)J recombination takes place during B-cell differentiation.
source: V(D)J recombination takes place during B-cell differentiation (Hozumi and Tonegawa, 1976; Schatz and Swanson, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: For each Ig chain, V, D, and J gene segments for the heavy chain, and V and J gene segments for the light chain, are randomly chosen and joined with random non-templated deletions and insertions at the junction, creating a long, hypervariable region, called the complementarity determining region 3 (CDR3).
source: For each Ig chain, V, D, and J gene segments for the heavy chain, and V and J gene segments for the light chain, are randomly chosen and joined with random non-templated deletions and insertions at the junction, creating a long, hypervariable region, called the complementarity determining region 3 (CDR3) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about VDJ recombination, also illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Somatic hypermutation consists primarily of point substitutions, as well as insertions and deletions, restricted to Ig-coding genes.
source: Somatic hypermutation consists primarily of point substitutions, as well as insertions and deletions, restricted to Ig-coding genes (Feng et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Members of the same clonal family usually share their specificities.
source: Since members of the same family usually share their specificities (De Boer et al., 2001), affinity maturation first competes families against each other for antigen binding in the early stages of the reaction, and then selects out the best binders within families in the later stages (Tas et al., 2016; Mesin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: It is generally unlikely that the same or a similar CDR3 sequence be generated independently multiple times.
source: it is generally unlikely that the same or a similar CDR3 sequence be generated independently multiple times (Elhanati et al., 2015; Ruiz Ortega et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The distribution of clonal family sizes follows a power-law with exponent –2.3.
source: The resulting distribution of clone sizes follows a power-law with exponent –2.3.
evidence: This is derived from data analysis of families identified in high-reliability regions.

claim: Only HILARy-CDR3, HILARy-full, and the alignment-free method achieve satisfactory performance (under an hour) for large VJl classes.
source: We find that only three methods achieve satisfactory performance (under an hour): the two methods introduced here, and the alignment-free method.
evidence: This is based on computational time measurements shown in Figure 4A.

claim: HILARy-full achieved 99.9% precision and 98.5% sensitivity for a typical repertoire.
source: In this task, HILARy-full achieved 99.9% precision and 98.5% sensitivity; partis 93% and 96.9%; and SCOPer 96.6% and 99.1%.
evidence: This is calculated by averaging over all CDR3 lengths in proportion of their abundance.

claim: Site frequency spectra are universal for all CDR3 lengths.
source: We find that site frequency spectra are universal for all CDR3 lengths, suggesting that the dynamics that give rise to the structure of lineages and the subsequent dynamics that influence the sampling of family members do not depend on the CDR3 length.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7B with data from donor 326651.

claim: Indel events within the CDR3 are rare and generally selected against.
source: Such indel events are rare and generally selected against (Lupo et al., 2022), therefore in what follows we shall assume the effect of these events is negligible.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The effect of V or J template alignment errors on identifying VJ classes is insignificant.
source: we previously found the effect of alignment errors to be insignificant for identifying VJ classes (Spisak et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: HILARy relies on the soNNia model, which is based on a neural network.
source: HILARy relies on the soNNia model, which is based on a neural network, and benefits from its expressivity to quantify the purifying selection that modifies the VDJ recombination statistics.
evidence: This describes the technical approach used in the method.

claim: The performance of the soNNia model is satisfactory when applied to healthy memory repertoires.
source: We found the performance of this model satisfactory when applied to healthy memory repertoires, in agreement with previous findings (Isacchini et al., 2021; Ruiz Ortega et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Single-linkage clustering outperforms state-of-the-art approaches for simulated samples based on real datasets with mutation rates ranging between 1.3% and 5.5%.
source: As demonstrated in Balashova et al., 2024, single-linkage clustering outperforms state-of-the-art approaches for simulated samples based on real datasets with mutation rates ranging between 1.3% and 5.5%.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Purifying selection is expected to be more pronounced in datasets of disease-specific cohorts.
source: Purifying selection is expected to be more pronounced in datasets of disease-specific cohorts and a default soNNia model may overestimate the diversity (Mayer and Callan, 2022) and lead to underestimation of the fallout rate.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research and represents an inference about model limitations.

claim: The dynamics of expansion, mutation, and selection are independent of the CDR3 and are dictated by the rules of affinity maturation and memory formation rather than BCR specificity.
source: This result implies that the dynamics of expansion, mutation, and selection are independent of the CDR3 and suggests they are dictated by the rules of affinity maturation and memory formation rather than BCR specificity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the universality of lineage statistics across CDR3 lengths.

claim: HILARy is distinguished by consistently high precision and high sensitivity across different junction lengths and levels of clonality, while being very fast compared to previous methods.
source: Using synthetic datasets we demonstrated it is distinguished by consistently high precision and high sensitivity across different junction lengths and levels of clonality, while very fast compared to previous methods.
evidence: This is supported by the benchmark results presented throughout the manuscript.
